title: The economics of parent-subsidiary mergers: an empirical analysis

rival_explanations: wealth redistribution from minority shareholders to the parent (rather than productive value gains)

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (publicly traded U.S. parent and majority-controlled subsidiary firms; subsidiaries typically operate in a different industry from the parent)
context.country_region: United States (NYSE, Amex, and Nasdaq listed firms)
context.sample_size: 105 parent-subsidiary mergers (105 subsidiaries and 101 parents) and 38 third party buyouts

data_sources.name: CRSP file (daily stock price returns; CRSP equally-weighted index)

analyses.label: Table 2, Panel A — parent-subsidiary mergers, two-day announcement excess returns

dv.name: two-day average excess return to subsidiaries and parents

key_ivs.name: parent-subsidiary merger announcement
key_ivs.measure: date of first public report of the event (announcement date)
key_ivs.source: Wall Street Journal and Dow Jones News Wire

analyses.label: Table 2, Panel B — parent-subsidiary mergers, daily excess returns

dv.name: daily excess returns around announcement
dv.measure: daily standardized prediction errors from the market model; also one-month interval excess return (not reported in table)

key_ivs.name: parent-subsidiary merger announcement
key_ivs.measure: days relative to date of first public report (day 0)
key_ivs.source: Wall Street Journal and Dow Jones News Wire

analyses.label: Sign test — ratio of minority gains vs parent ownership proportion (105 matched pairs)

dv.name: gains ratio to minority shareholders vs ownership proportion
dv.measure: two-day excess return times pre-merger market value times proportion of shares not held by parent; treated as 105 matched pairs of gains ratio and ownership proportion, sign test

analyses.label: Table 3 — post-merger restructuring developments (5-year follow-up categorization)

dv.name: post-merger restructuring category
dv.measure: delineation of subsequent developments into restructured (73 events, 70%) vs no evidence of restructuring (32 events, 30%), with sub-categories

analyses.label: Cross-sectional regressions of excess returns on restructuring-category dummies (not reported in tables)

dv.name: [withheld: wording matches the source]
dv.measure: two-day market-model excess returns specified as a function of qualitative variables reflecting categories of subsequent restructuring activities

key_ivs.name: restructuring-category qualitative variables
key_ivs.measure: dummy variables for categories of subsequent restructuring activities

analyses.label: Table 4, Panel A — third party buyouts, two-day announcement excess returns

dv.name: two-day average excess return to subsidiaries and parents in third party buyouts
dv.measure: market-model two-day (-1,0) excess returns; includes difference-in-means t-test and Mann-Whitney test vs parent-subsidiary mergers

key_ivs.name: third party buyout announcement
key_ivs.measure: date of first public report of the buyout
key_ivs.source: Wall Street Journal and Dow Jones News Wire

analyses.label: Litigation filings event study — share-price responses to 27 lawsuit filings

dv.name: [withheld: wording matches the source]
dv.measure: market-model two-day excess returns at announcements of 27 lawsuit filings

key_ivs.name: shareholder lawsuit filing
key_ivs.measure: frequency of litigation determined by examining Wall Street Journal for shareholder lawsuits during transaction period (32 lawsuits among 105 mergers)

analyses.label: Weinberger v UOP decision announcement event study
analyses.shock_or_instrument: Weinberger v UOP Delaware Supreme Court decision (Feb 7, 1983)
analyses.sample: 60 majority-controlled subsidiaries and parents publicly traded at time of decision

dv.name: [withheld: wording matches the source]
dv.measure: market-model two-day excess returns at announcement of the Delaware Supreme Court Weinberger v UOP decision reported February 7, 1983

key_ivs.name: Weinberger v UOP court decision
key_ivs.measure: announcement of the decision on February 7, 1983 in the New York Times and Legal Times

analyses.label: Table 5 — two-day excess returns disaggregated by approval status, Weinberger, means of payment, origin

dv.name: [withheld: wording matches the source]
dv.measure: market-model two-day excess returns disaggregated by merger approval status (majority-of-minority vs simple majority), Weinberger decision (before/after), means of payment (equity/cash), and origin of subsidiary; with difference-in-means t-tests

key_ivs.name: merger approval status
key_ivs.measure: majority of minority required (N=21) vs simple majority (N=84)

analyses.label: Equation (1) — weighted least squares regression of subsidiary two-day return on CASH and POST-Weinberger
Origin-status subsample returns — partial acquisition vs partial divestiture

dv.name: [withheld: wording matches the source]
dv.measure: market-model two-day excess returns for units originating by partial acquisition vs partial divestiture, with difference tests

key_ivs.name: subsidiary origin status
key_ivs.measure: partial acquisition vs partial divestiture (equity carve-outs / partial spin-offs)

analyses.label: Parent excess returns at original partial-divestiture announcement (28 events)
analyses.sample: 28 partial divestitures among 48 parents that reacquire full ownership

dv.name: two-day excess return to parents at original partial divestiture
dv.measure: market-model two-day excess returns to parents at announcements of the original partial divestiture; further split into 21 positive-return and 7 negative-return subsamples

key_ivs.name: original partial-divestiture announcement
key_ivs.measure: origin announcement dates reported in Wall Street Journal for 28 partial divestitures with parent data on CRSP daily return file
